newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN to appeal for $260 mln for east Zaire relief.
newsitem.headline: UN to appeal for $260 mln for east Zaire relief.

text.p: The United Nations will launch an emergency appeal on Monday for $260 million to fund relief operations in eastern Zaire and Rwanda, a U.N. official said.
Spokeswoman Madeleine Moulan-Acevedo of the U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs (DHA) told Reuters the consolidated appeal by U.N. agencies would be launched out of New York.
Half a million Rwandan Hutu refugees returned home from Goma in east Zaire according to the U.N. refugee agency after Tutsi rebel shelling of Mugunga camp forced Hutu militia to flee.
Over a million Hutus fled Rwanda in mid-1994 after a rebel Tutsi army overran the country following the genocide of Tutsis by Hutu extremists. Many ended up in camps in eastern Zaire.
The sudden flood of Hutus to Africa's most crowded country has caught aid agencies off-guard and will put new pressures on the international community to assist them in their communes.

Housing is likely to emerge as a key problem since many homes belonging to the refugees have been occupied by diaspora Tutsis -- 800,000 of whom returned home, almost a one-to-one replacement of the genocide dead, after Tutsis swept to power.

The refugees will need tools and seeds to get back into the agricultural cycle, as well as international monitoring in remote villages where many could face Tutsi allegations of participation in the genocide.

Diplomats expect a surge in arrests and say lack of prison space will be one problem confronting the donors. Some 90,000 Hutus accused of genocide are jammed into Rwanda's overcrowded jails, up from 18,000 early in 1995, and the starts of trials have been repeatedly delayed.
